ἀνοικ-ίζω ,
A.remove up the country, ἀ. τὴν Σπάρτην, i.e. break it up as a city, Arist. Rh.Al. 1423a7 ; “ἀ. τινὰς ἐς τὴν Περσίδα”
Paus. 1.25.5
, cf. Str. 13.3.3 ; ἀ. [τέττιγας] φθόνου ἐς δένδρα remove them out of envy's way, dub. in
Philostr. VA 7.11 (leg. ἀπ-):— Pass. and Med. , shift one's dwelling up the country, migrate inland or to higher ground,
“αὐτοὶ δ᾽ ἀνῳκίσανθ᾽ ὅπως ἀνωτάτω”
Ar. Pax 207
, cf. Av. 1351 , Str. 9.2.17 , App. Pun. 84 ; and of cities, to be built inland or away from the coast,
Th. 1.7 :—generally, migrate,
“ἀνοικίσασθαι εἰς Ὄλυνθον”
Id. 1.58
, cf. 8.31 .
II. resettle, colonize afresh,
Paus. 2.1.2 , Memn. 60 ( Med. ); rebuild, Aps. pp.239,245 H.:— Pass. , to be repeopled,
Plu. Luc. 29 .
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
